title: Homework: Helpful or Harmful?
text:
Many people believe that homework should be banned in primary schools. In my view, this idea is misguided. Children need regular practice to strengthen what they learn in class. However, the amount of work should be reasonable, so teachers must consider how much time pupils spend on each task.

Critics argue that homework leaves little time for play and family life. Although this concern is valid, a short daily task can actually build discipline and independence. Ultimately, the real issue is not whether homework exists, but how well it is designed.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do children need?
options: Regular practice to strengthen what they learn

questions.text: What do critics of homework argue?
options: It is too expensive for schools
It leaves little time for play and family life

questions.text: What can be inferred about the writer's position on homework?
options: They support homework, but want it to be reasonable
They think teachers should not assign any work
They are neutral and offer no opinion

questions.text: Why does the writer say the real issue is how homework is designed?
options: Because they think homework is not needed at all
Because they believe well-designed homework can be beneficial
Because critics are wrong about everything
Because teachers prefer to design homework

paragraph_translations: Birçok insan, ilkokullarda ev ödevinin yasaklanması gerektiğine inanıyor. Bana göre bu fikir yanlış yönlendirilmiş. Çocukların sınıfta öğrendiklerini pekiştirmek için düzenli pratiğe ihtiyacı var. Ancak ödevin miktarı makul olmalı; bu yüzden öğretmenler öğrencilerin her göreve ne kadar zaman harcadığını göz önünde bulundurmalı.

Eleştirmenler, ev ödevinin oyun ve aile hayatı için çok az zaman bıraktığını savunuyor. Bu kaygı geçerli olsa da, kısa ve günlük bir görev aslında disiplin ve bağımsızlık kazandırabilir. Sonuçta asıl mesele ödevin var olup olmaması değil, ne kadar iyi tasarlandığıdır.
